children: none, because the field, the door check and the migration are one seam over one store. The migration is not a separable child — a field added without migrating the 263 leaves the corpus in two shapes, which is worse than either shape alone.
workflow_and_state: code-seam@v2: THINKME -> TICKETME -> BUILDME -> PROVEME -> WATCHME(the-author-field-holds-more-than-one-name) -> PROVED -> [SUPERSEDED]

watchme.carrier: a verdict artifact against this ticket's falsifier: tickets carrying author, tickets carrying via, distinct author values, distinct via values, and the count of unresolvable-and-saying-so
watchme.consumer: whoever routes a correction back to the hand that made a ticket, and Akien, who asked the question that cast this
watchme.enough: DELIBERATELY NOT SATISFIABLE BY PRESENCE. The watch clears only when the corpus holds at least 2 DISTINCT author values across at least 20 tickets — because the failure this ticket names is a field that reads CC forever, which presence alone cannot distinguish from a field nobody thought about. Until a second writer exists the watch stands open and SAYS SO, reporting the distinct-value count rather than clearing green on 263/263 populated. This is the ticket's own falsifier honoured rather than rounded off.
watchme.nexus: the tickets store's tree — the corpus's own record of who makes it
watchme.trigger: each ticket cast through the /sorted door, plus a corpus sweep at each build_inspector run
